name: Yala National Park
description: Yala National Park, located in the Hambanthota District of Sri Lanka, is a protected area known for its rich biodiversity and wildlife, particularly elephants. Established in 1908, it was originally a hunting ground. Today, visitors can enjoy jeep safaris through its dense jungles, where they have the chance to see over 200 species of birds, as well as endangered Asian elephants, leopards, and various other animals. Notable events include the annual Elephant Gathering, where hundreds of elephants gather at Yala during the dry season.
mobile_signal: Good near main entrance; weak inside park
activities: Jeep safaris, Elephant watching, Bird watching
ticket_price: USD 25-45 (foreign adult) + service charge + 18% VAT; LKR ~60 (local adult)
wheelchair_access: limited - mostly jeep safari based; visitor center is accessible
monsoon_note: Block 1 sometimes closes briefly during heavy NE monsoon (Oct-Jan) flooding; park stays open most of year

name: Bundala National Park
description: Bundala National Park, nestled in the southeastern corner of Sri Lanka, is a crucial sanctuary for migratory birds. Established as a nature reserve in 1986, it offers visitors an opportunity to observe over 200 species of birds, including the critically endangered Greater Adjutant Stork. The park's rich biodiversity makes it a significant site for bird enthusiasts and nature lovers. Historically, the area has been inhabited by various indigenous communities, and today, it remains an important stopover for millions of birds migrating between Asia and Africa.

name: Lunugamvehera National Park
description: Lunugamvehera National Park, nestled in the southernmost tip of Sri Lanka, offers visitors a chance to witness diverse wildlife including elephants, birds, and various native species. Established as a nature reserve in 1968, it covers an area of over 200 square kilometers. The park is particularly famous for its bird watching tours, where tourists can observe over 250 species of birds. Elephant watching safaris are also popular, allowing visitors to see these majestic creatures in their natural habitat. Guided nature walks through the park provide insights into the rich biodiversity and ecological balance of the region.
activities: Bird Watching, Elephant Watching, Nature Walks

name: Ussangoda National Park
description: Ussangoda National Park, nestled in the southeastern coast of Hambanthota, offers visitors a unique blend of natural beauty and archaeological interest. Established as a national park in 2018, it encompasses a vast stretch of coastline and mangrove forests, providing an ideal setting for beach relaxation and coastal walks. The park's name commemorates the ancient Ussangoda site, which holds significant archaeological importance, revealing evidence of early human settlements along this ancient trade route. Visitors can explore the park's trails, learn about the rich history through guided tours, and enjoy panoramic views of the Indian Ocean.
activities: Beach Relaxation, Coastal Scenic Walk, Archaeological Exploration

name: Kalametiya Sanctuary
description: Kalametiya Sanctuary, nestled in the Hambanthota District of Sri Lanka, offers visitors a unique opportunity to observe a diverse array of bird species. Established as a sanctuary to protect local avian life, it attracts bird watchers and nature enthusiasts year-round. Boasting clear blue waters and lush greenery, the sanctuary also features canoeing tours, allowing visitors to explore its tranquil waters while spotting wildlife up close. Its rich biodiversity and serene setting make it a significant natural haven in the region, preserving Sri Lanka’s ecological balance.
wheelchair_access: limited - accessible only at the lagoon viewing area
monsoon_note: Important bird sanctuary; lagoon levels and bird activity peak in dry season Mar-Sep

name: Wirawila-Tissa Sanctuary
description: Wirawila-Tissa Sanctuary is a serene sanctuary nestled in the Southern Province, known for its diverse wildlife and lush greenery. This protected area offers visitors a chance to observe birds and other native species in their natural habitat, making it a must-visit spot for nature enthusiasts.
wheelchair_access: limited - accessible via tank bund path

name: Hambantota Herbal Park
description: The Hambantota Herbal Park, part of a former tea estate, offers visitors a unique blend of nature and tranquility. It features a collection of medicinal and aromatic plants, providing an immersive experience for those interested in herbal remedies and wellness. The park also includes a tea plantation tour, allowing guests to learn about the cultivation process and taste freshly brewed teas. For those seeking inner peace, guided meditation sessions are available, while photography enthusiasts can capture the serene landscapes and vibrant flora. Notable for its rich biodiversity and cultural significance, the park attracts both local and international tourists.

name: Tissamaharama Organic Farm
description: Tissamaharama Organic Farm, nestled in the lush tea estates of Hambanthota, offers visitors a chance to explore its sprawling organic tea gardens while learning about sustainable farming practices. The farm also features a farm shop where one can purchase locally made products, providing an opportunity to support local artisans and businesses. Established over a decade ago by a group of passionate farmers committed to preserving traditional methods alongside modern sustainability, the farm has become a hub for eco-conscious tourism, attracting both locals and tourists seeking a glimpse into sustainable agriculture practices.
activities: Explore the organic tea gardens, Learn about sustainable farming practices, Visit the farm shop for locally made products

name: Sooriyawewa Spice Trail
description: The Sooriyawewa Spice Trail is a unique tea estate located in the picturesque Hambanthota district of Sri Lanka. Known for its high-quality tea and diverse spice plantations, visitors can enjoy a tea tasting experience while learning about the estate’s rich history and culture. The trail offers a glimpse into the local way of life, with tours through spice gardens and tea fields, perfect for those interested in both tea culture and natural wonders. Notable for its scenic views and educational opportunities, it attracts tourists eager to immerse themselves in the authentic flavors and traditions of Sri Lankan tea and spices.
activities: Tea tasting, Spice plantation tour, Photography
monsoon_note: May–Aug SW monsoon; A2 highway may flood

name: Suriyawewa Botanics
description: Suriyawewa Botanics, a serene tea estate in Hambanthota, offers visitors a glimpse into the lush green landscapes of Sri Lanka's tea plantations. The estate, established in the early 20th century, is known for its unique collection of rare tea plants and traditional practices passed down through generations. Guided tours allow guests to explore the scenic tea gardens, learn about the art of tea making, and take in the breathtaking views of the Indian Ocean. Cultural highlights include a visit to the estate's museum, showcasing artifacts and photographs that trace the rich history of tea cultivation in Sri Lanka. Tea enthusiasts can sample freshly brewed teas, while nature lovers can marvel at the diverse flora and fauna.
activities: Tea plantation tour, Photography, Tea tasting

name: Lunugamvehera Herb Walk
description: Lunugamvehera Herb Walk is a unique tea estate in Hambanthota, Sri Lanka, offering visitors a chance to explore its lush gardens while learning about its diverse range of herbs. This estate, known for its high-quality tea production, also serves as a sanctuary for over 300 species of medicinal plants. Visitors can take a guided tour to learn about the history of the tea plantation and its herb garden, which was established by the local community in the early 20th century. The herb walk includes a section dedicated to traditional Sri Lankan teas and herbal remedies, making it a perfect spot for those interested in both tea culture and natural health.
activities: Herb identification, Tea plantation tour, Herbal tea tasting

name: Ridiyagama Estate
description: Ridiyagama Estate, nestled in the lush tea lands of Hambanthota, offers visitors a chance to explore the verdant tea gardens and learn about the meticulous tea-making process. The estate's panoramic views provide a serene backdrop to this unique experience, blending natural beauty with cultural heritage. Historically significant as one of the first estates established in the region, it played a crucial role in the development of tea cultivation in Sri Lanka. Visitors can appreciate the rich history while enjoying the tranquility of the estate.
activities: Explore tea gardens, Learn about tea-making process, Enjoy panoramic views
monsoon_note: May–Aug SW monsoon; A2 highway may flood
